root_cause.text: In the amdgpu device cleanup paths, `amdgpu_device_set_cg_state()` and `amdgpu_device_set_pg_state()` iterated over `adev->ip_blocks` and dereferenced `adev->ip_blocks[i].version` without verifying it was initialized, so a failed GPU init that left some IP block version pointers NULL caused a NULL pointer dereference during teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that “IP blocks may have a NULL version pointer” after initialization fails, and the patch adds `if (!adev->ip_blocks[i].version) continue;` in both `amdgpu_device_set_cg_state` and `amdgpu_device_set_pg_state` before any `version->type` access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a null-pointer guard in CG state handling to skip unversioned IP blocks.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in amdgpu_device_set_cg_state() to skip processing an IP block when adev->ip_blocks[i].version is NULL, inserted immediately after the existing late_initialized check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now avoids dereferencing or using IP blocks that do not have a valid version pointer, preventing invalid access and ensuring only properly initialized blocks participate in CG state handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip IP blocks without a valid version when setting power-gating state to avoid operating on uninitialized entries.
intent_record.what: In amdgpu_device_set_pg_state(), a new conditional check was added after the late_initialized check: if adev->ip_blocks[i].version is null, the loop continues and skips that IP block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, power-gating state changes will no longer attempt to access or use an IP block's version field when it has not been set, preventing invalid dereferences or unintended handling of uninitialized blocks.

grouping_result.intent: Skip IP blocks without a valid version when setting power-gating state to avoid operating on uninitialized entries.

consistency_review.core_intent: Skip IP blocks without a valid version when handling CG/power-gating state to avoid operating on uninitialized entries.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they add null checks in amdgpu_device_set_cg_state() and amdgpu_device_set_pg_state() to skip IP blocks whose version pointer was uninitialized, preventing the NULL pointer dereference during cleanup.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is immediately followed by dereferences of adev->ip_blocks[i].version->type without first checking whether version is initialized. The missing NULL guard in this cleanup path is the direct cause of the NULL pointer dereference.

This statement begins the branch that dereferences adev->ip_blocks[i].version->type later in the same condition chain. Because uninitialized IP block version pointers were not checked, teardown could hit a NULL dereference here.

This existing guard only checks late_initialized status, but not whether adev->ip_blocks[i].version is valid. The bug arises because the code proceeds past this check and later dereferences version unconditionally.
This guard is insufficient to protect the subsequent version->type access. Failed GPU initialization can leave version NULL even when this status check passes, leading to the cleanup-time crash.

vuln_statements.explanation: This guard only checks late_initialized and does not verify adev->ip_blocks[i].version is non-NULL. The cleanup path can still proceed to later dereference version->type, which is the root cause of the NULL pointer dereference when GPU init failed partway.

This condition starts the branch in the cleanup logic that later dereferences adev->ip_blocks[i].version->type without first ensuring version was initialized. When some IP blocks have NULL version pointers after failed initialization, this path can trigger the NULL pointer dereference.
